analysis.title: Hyperscaler Test / UK Inflation & Wages / EU-China Trade / Korea GDP / Israel Election
key_insights: Alphabet (GOOGL) and Microsoft (MSFT) report Wednesday and Amazon (AMZN) reports Thursday. Investors want evidence that hyperscaler revenue and cash flow can keep pace with accelerating capex and higher funding costs. GE Vernova (GEV) and Vertiv (VRT) also report Wednesday as a read-across for power and behind-the-meter demand.

The setup into hyperscaler earnings is described as binary. Monetization catching up with infrastructure spending could drive a sharp rebound in AI and power/data-center beneficiaries. Slowing cloud growth plus another capex step-up would support the bear case that spending is running ahead of returns.

US hedge funds de-risked again last week, concentrated in AI. Selling moved from semis to hyperscalers, with the strongest two-day reduction in hyperscaler longs since covid, before funds reversed Friday. Net exposure fell to the 17th percentile on a 1y lookback, which raises short-squeeze potential on better-than-expected earnings.

UBS Rates Trading says the market prices near-term Fed patience, but sticky inflation and AI capex leave terminal-rate risks skewed higher. The desk recommends fading the recent 7y richening and expectations for cuts to long-end Treasury issuance.

UK BRC shop-price inflation rose to 2.1% y/y in October from 1.4%, the fastest since February 2024. Food inflation rose to 2.9% from 2.5% and non-food inflation to 1.7% from 0.8%. The BRC says retailers' cost buffers are eroding. Official UK CPI was 3.5% in September.

UK Chancellor Healey is reported to be set to announce a 3.9% rise in the National Living Wage to about GBP13.20 from GBP12.71, above current inflation of 3.5%. The 18-20 rate would rise to about GBP11.27 from GBP10.85.

In euro rates, OATs are driving the market. The long end started flattening aggressively mid last week as betas to 1y1y broke down. The desk prefers basis wideners through anticipated volatility in an event-heavy week.

The EU is considering quotas or tariffs on Chinese chemicals, furniture and machinery as early as Q1 2027 to narrow a goods deficit of EUR360 bn. UBS Wealth Management CIO says this may add trade friction and favor companies with strong balance sheets, pricing power and diversified supply chains. The CIO forecasts 15% Eurozone earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027.
China's industrial profits rose 14.4% y/y in September, up from 4.2% in August, and 15.5% in January-September. Computer, communication and electronic equipment profits rose 103.8% year to date.

South Korea Q3 GDP rose 1% q/q against a 0.7% consensus, driven by exports (+2.3% q/q) and facility investment (+4.1%). Private consumption fell 0.2%, annual growth slowed to 3.4% from 3.7%, and October consumer sentiment fell 1.2 points to 105.4. The stronger print could prompt a BoK forecast upgrade.

Israel's election exit polls are due 20:00 London Tuesday. A bloc with 56-57 or more of 120 seats and a 4-5 seat lead would likely reduce post-election uncertainty. The last poll average has the Eizenkot camp at 53 seats and Netanyahu's at 51. Two parties near the 3.25% threshold, Reservists and Amcha Yisrael, are worth watching.

The RBNZ is all but certain to hike from 2.75% on Wednesday. The desk expects the terminal rate near neutral (3-3.5%) and likes holding received 1y1y. Risks are positioning, the Nov. 7 election and the trade-weighted NZ dollar.
The FX desk favors short AUDNZD, especially if Wednesday's Australian CPI squeezes it toward 1.2360-1.2370, with a wider stop above 1.2500. CPI lands 30 minutes before the RBNZ decision.
Chile's central bank is likely to hold at 4.50% Tuesday. Oil prices and El Niño are upside inflation risks and weak activity pulls the other way. UBS forecasts Thursday's unemployment at 9.6%.

UBS FX Sales expects unwinding of BRLMXN longs to support the Mexican peso, though it calls Mexican fundamentals poor. Banxico may turn more hawkish or drop its easing bias given hot data and the speed of MXN depreciation.

Gold is structurally bullish and tactically cautious, with strong China physical demand. Silver is headline-sensitive with downside risk below 56.27. DeMark technicals are bullish on gold and neutral on silver and platinum.

Japan equities rose on AI enthusiasm. Ibiden gained 10.8%, Advantest 9.4%, Lasertec 4.6% and SUMCO 4.5%. Mitsubishi Estate and Mitsui Fudosan each fell 3.5% and Daiichi Sankyo fell 7% on ADC study data.

Celestica rose more than 10% after hours. Q3 revenue was $5.83 bn and EPS $3.26 against consensus of $5.46 bn and $2.97. FY2027 outlook of $40 bn revenue and $21.50 EPS beat consensus of $35.84 bn and $19.60, and FY2026 guidance was raised.

US equities re-risked sharply as long-only demand and hedge-fund gross restoration combined with lower volatility. UBS Equity Derivatives calls the move positioning-led rather than fundamental. November S&P 500 implied volatility fell 75bp and skew flattened.

USTs twist flattened. A 2y auction tailed marginally despite record direct participation. The 10y yield was little changed at 4.99% and 2s10s and 5s30s flattened 4bp. A $70 bn 5y auction and the FOMC follow. SOFR pricing shows about 3bp for the October FOMC, 23bp cumulative into December and 70bp by mid-2027.
